title: Career Roadmap · Catalogue Executive
summary: A Catalogue Executive manages the product information displayed on e-commerce websites and online marketplaces. The role involves creating and updating product listings, writing product descriptions, maintaining product attributes, uploading images, checking prices and inventory information, and ensuring products comply with each platform's listing requirements.

about.label: Primary sectors
about.text: E-commerce, online retail, digital marketplaces, D2C brands

about.label: Work environment
about.text: E-commerce offices, retail operations teams, marketplace management agencies and remote or hybrid teams

blocks.text: A Catalogue Executive manages the product information displayed on e-commerce websites and online marketplaces. The role involves creating and updating product listings, writing product descriptions, maintaining product attributes, uploading images, checking prices and inventory information, and ensuring products comply with each platform's listing requirements.
Catalogue Executives help customers find and understand products while ensuring that online product information is accurate, consistent and easy to navigate.

For example, when a company sells 500 products on Amazon, Flipkart or its own website, the Catalogue Executive ensures each product has the correct title, description, category, specifications, images, variations and other required details.

rows.text: Upload listings, validate information and correct basic errors
Manage product listings, attributes, variations and marketplace updates
Handle bulk catalogues, listing quality, audits and platform-specific issues
E-Commerce Operations Manager / Catalogue Team Lead
Manage catalogue teams, listing processes, quality standards and operational performance

blocks.text: Career progression depends on platform expertise, accuracy, productivity, communication skills and experience with large product catalogues.
The following plan assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adapt it to the institution's actual course structure.
Year 1
Foundation
Learn e-commerce and product-content fundamentals

items.text: Understand e-commerce business models, online retail and digital marketplaces.
Learn product titles, descriptions, attributes, SKUs, categories and variants.
Practise professional product-description writing.
Develop Excel or Google Sheets skills, including sorting, filtering and data validation.
Understand image requirements, product specifications and basic image editing.
Learn proofreading, spelling consistency and product-data quality checks.

blocks.text: Year 2
Specialisation
Develop marketplace management skills

items.text: Learn seller dashboards and listing workflows on relevant marketplaces.
Understand product categorisation, parent-child variations and bulk uploads.
Practise managing price, stock, dimensions, specifications and product images.
Learn listing optimisation, keyword research and basic product SEO.
Understand marketplace listing policies and restricted product requirements.
Learn to identify duplicate listings, missing attributes and content errors.
Explore Shopify or another e-commerce content management system.

blocks.text: Year 3
Job readiness
Build operational and analytical capability

items.text: Manage a simulated catalogue containing hundreds of product records.
Practise bulk upload preparation, validation and error correction.
Create product-content standards and catalogue quality checklists.
Use spreadsheets to measure listing completeness, error rates and turnaround time.
Learn basic automation for repetitive data-cleaning tasks.
Complete an internship with an e-commerce seller, D2C brand, retailer or marketplace agency.
Prepare a portfolio with sample listings, a cleaned catalogue and a quality audit report.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Build a 100-product catalogue
Create a spreadsheet for a fictional online store with SKU, product name, brand, category, price, specifications, stock status and image filename. Include consistent data types and validation rules.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Create marketplace-ready product listings

Prepare 20 product listings for a selected category, such as apparel, electronics or home goods. Write clear titles and descriptions, organise attributes and follow the chosen platform's published requirements.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Product listing optimisation

Improve 10 sample listings by refining titles, product attributes and descriptions. Document what changed and explain how the changes could improve clarity and discoverability without making unsupported product claims.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Catalogue quality audit
Create a dataset containing intentional errors, such as missing SKUs, duplicate records, invalid prices and incomplete attributes. Detect, correct and report the errors using Excel or Python.

blocks.label: Project 5
blocks.text: Catalogue performance dashboard
Build an Excel or Power BI dashboard showing total listings, complete listings, error rate, pending uploads, rejection reasons and average correction time using sample data.

blocks.text: AI tools can accelerate drafting and data processing, but every product detail must be checked against a reliable source. Incorrect dimensions, ingredients, compatibility claims or other specifications can mislead customers and create compliance problems.

By the end of the B.Voc programme, the student should aim to have:

items.text: Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.
The ability to create accurate, structured product listings.
Familiarity with SKUs, categories, attributes, variants and bulk uploads.
Basic knowledge of marketplace listing policies and product SEO.
Experience identifying and correcting catalogue errors.
A sample catalogue of at least 100 products.
A quality-audit report and catalogue dashboard.
An internship or simulated project demonstrating practical workflow knowledge.

blocks.text: Final recommendation

For a Catalogue Executive role, prioritise spreadsheet proficiency, product-data accuracy, marketplace listing workflows and content quality. Build a portfolio that proves you can manage product information systematically, not merely write descriptions. Adding marketplace SEO, basic analytics and catalogue automation skills can help you progress into higher-responsibility e-commerce operations roles.
